title: Triaging a log
purpose: Reads a CI console, a Maven, npm or dotnet build, or a test run, and returns what's worth reading: the error and warning lines grouped by signature, with numbers, ids, timestamps and hex replaced so the same complaint counts once. Each group has its count, its first and last line, one sample, and the Java, .NET, Node or Python stack trace that belongs to it.
inputs: A log file in the workspace, stdin, or `--text`. `--since`, `--level error` and `--grep` narrow it, `--context` adds the lines around each sample, and `--max-groups` caps the list, saying so when it does.
verifies: Every line number it reports is read again from the file to confirm it holds the sample, the group counts are added up against the lines it matched, and the bytes read are compared with the file's size.
limits: Lines it couldn't classify are counted and reported, never dropped. Past 2,000 distinct signatures, matched lines are counted but not grouped, which keeps memory constant. A file streams however large; stdin and `--text` are held in memory, up to 64 MiB.
